subject.title: [Bug]: CLI relay exits silently with code 1 when session lane is blocked — no timeout or busy error surfaced

question: Should Gateway-backed CLI agent dispatches return a terminal session-lane-busy result after the wait threshold, and should that use a distinct exit code or keep exit code 1 with clear stderr/JSON?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the candidate fix changes the delivery contract for blocked CLI dispatches rather than only improving a log message.

options.title: Land terminal CLI busy result
options.body: Make CLI-originated same-session lane waits surface LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED with actionable stderr/JSON and a maintainer-chosen exit code.

options.title: Keep queued execution and improve timeout text
options.body: Keep the current eventual-queue behavior but ensure timeout or failure paths always print a clear diagnostic.

options.title: Pause for broader queue policy
options.body: Hold this issue and the linked PR until maintainers decide whether CLI callers should get a force-queue or explicit wait mode.

recommendation.title: Land terminal CLI busy result
recommendation.body: Make CLI-originated same-session lane waits surface LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED with actionable stderr/JSON and a maintainer-chosen exit code.

likelyOwner.reason: The Gateway-backed CLI relay and queue-hardening history make this the best available owner for the CLI delivery-contract decision.
